sentences.text: Octavian was born in Rome on 23 September 63 BC.
His father was Gaius Octavius, a member of the Senate, Rome's governing council, whose members sat for life.
sentences.evidence: Suetonius, Augustus 4.1 (for a family that had already produced several senators)

sentences.text: His mother, Atia, was the daughter of Marcus Atius Balbus and of Iulia.
Iulia was the sister of Gaius Iulius Caesar, a politician and general, so Octavian was Caesar's great-nephew.
In the summer of 59 BC Gaius Octavius was returning from his province, a territory outside Italy that he had governed.
He died suddenly and unexpectedly at Nola, a town in Campania, a region of Italy.
Gaius Octavius left his son a large fortune.
Octavian was sickly from youth.
sentences.evidence: Suetonius, Augustus 80-82; Nikolaos of Damascus, Life of Caesar 14f. and 19-21.

sentences.text: A year after Gaius Octavius died, Atia married Lucius Marcius Philippus.
Philippus, now Octavian's stepfather, came from one of the leading families of Rome.
In 51 BC Caesar was finishing the conquest of the region of Gaul.
sentences.evidence: Suetonius, Augustus 8.1; Quintilian 12.6.1; Nicolaus of Damascus, Life of Caesar 3

sentences.text: In 51 BC Caesar's sister Iulia, Octavian's grandmother, died.
Octavian gave the funeral speech for his grandmother Iulia.
sentences.evidence: Suetonius, Augustus 8.1; Quintilian 12.6.1; Nicolaus of Damascus, Life of Caesar 3
sentences.dispute: The ancient writer Nicolaus says Octavian was 9 when he gave the speech. Scholars say this is wrong.

sentences.text: In it he reminded the public of how old and famous the Julian family, Caesar's family, was.
Caesar's opponents planned to recall him from Gaul as early as possible.
He would then have to stand for election in Rome while holding no office.
Then his opponents would put him on trial in Rome for the many laws he had broken in his first term in the highest office, and have him convicted.
On 7 January 49 BC the decision to recall Caesar from Gaul was passed.
Caesar answered at once by starting a civil war against his enemies.
Caesar took the whole Italian peninsula within 2 months.
Caesar's opponents had won over Pompeius, a general who until then had been Caesar's political partner.
Caesar forced Pompeius and the government of Rome to flee across the Adriatic Sea.
When the civil war broke out, Octavian's mother and stepfather sent him out of Rome to safety on a country estate that had been his father's.
sentences.evidence: Nicolaus of Damascus, Life of Caesar 7

sentences.text: When the campaign in Italy was over and Pompeius and the government had fled, Octavian returned to Rome.
sentences.evidence: Nicolaus of Damascus, Life of Caesar 7

sentences.text: On 9 August 48 BC Caesar won the decisive battle of Pharsalus in Thessaly, a region of Greece.
At 15 years old Octavian received a priest's place on the board that led the Roman state religion.
sentences.evidence: Nicolaus of Damascus, Life of Caesar 9

sentences.text: The place had fallen vacant when Lucius Domitius Ahenobarbus, an opponent of Caesar, died in the battle of Pharsalus.
On 18 October 48 BC Octavian put on the robe of a citizen in a solemn ceremony on the Forum, the square where Rome's courts and politics were held.
sentences.evidence: Feriale Cumanum (ILS 108,5) gives the day and month; the year follows from Octavius holding the city prefecture in spring 47 at the Feriae Latinae, which presupposes he was already declared of age
sentences.dispute: The ancient writer Nicolaus says Octavian put on the robe of a citizen at about 14. Scholars say Nicolaus is mistaken.

sentences.text: With this he was declared an adult.
In the spring of 47 BC Rome's elected officials left the city for one day to sacrifice to the god Jupiter at a festival in the Alban Hills outside Rome.
sentences.evidence: Nicolaus of Damascus, Life of Caesar 13

sentences.text: For that day Octavian, not yet 16, stood in for the consuls, the two annual heads of the state.
Caesar returned to Rome at the beginning of October 47 BC.
In December 47 BC Caesar set out for North Africa.
He went to crush a new army gathered there by the republicans, his opponents in the civil war, who fought for the Republic, the rule of the Senate and of officials elected each year.
Octavian wanted to go with Caesar and learn war under him.
sentences.evidence: Nicolaus of Damascus, Life of Caesar 14-15

items.question: By the end of December 47 BC, has Octavian gone with Caesar to North Africa?

items.sentence: Iulia was the sister of Gaius Iulius Caesar, a politician and general, so Octavian was Caesar's great-nephew.

items.text: A patron who leaves for war.

main.title: Klaus Bringmann, Augustus (wbg Theiss, Darmstadt 2018, special edition of the 2nd, revised edition of 2012; first edition Primus 2007)
main.span: chapter I, section 1, to the end of chapter V
main.pages: Each page is the chapter, section and paragraph of this copy, which prints no page numbers: "II.1 ¶7" is chapter II, section 1, paragraph 7.

accounts.secondNote: The second account named for this life, Wardle’s Suetonius (Oxford 2014), is not to hand; the copy to hand is another edition. So, as Part II says for a job no account can do, every claim is contested.

letters.title: Res Gestae Divi Augusti, translated by Thomas Bushnell (2002)
letters.note: His own letters are not to hand. The stand-in, an inscription he set up, was written in AD 14, after every decision, so no lesson carries a letter.

telling.text: Caesar went to Africa; he stayed.
